label: Complete and Function Spaces
notes: Open the chapter, which spans printed pages 261 through 291. We study completeness, the property that Cauchy sequences converge, and the spaces of continuous functions that completeness makes tractable. These ideas connect topology to analysis through completion, the Arzela-Ascoli theorem, and the topologies of uniform and compact convergence on function spaces.

label: Complete Metric Spaces
notes: A metric space is complete when every Cauchy sequence converges within it. The real line is complete while the rationals are not. Completeness is not a topological invariant, since homeomorphic spaces may differ in it, but it is exactly the condition under which the contraction mapping principle and many existence theorems apply.

label: Completion
notes: Every metric space embeds isometrically as a dense subset of a complete metric space, its completion, which is unique up to isometry. The construction takes equivalence classes of Cauchy sequences. This is how the reals arise from the rationals and how abstract function spaces acquire the completeness analysis requires.

label: The Arzela-Ascoli Theorem
notes: The Arzela-Ascoli theorem characterizes compact subsets of the space of continuous functions on a compact domain: a family is relatively compact in the uniform topology exactly when it is pointwise bounded and equicontinuous. This is the central compactness criterion of analysis, underlying existence proofs for differential equations.

label: Topologies on Function Spaces
notes: On the set of functions between spaces we compare topologies: pointwise convergence, uniform convergence, and the compact-open topology that interpolates between them. The compact-open topology makes evaluation continuous and is the natural one for mapping spaces, central to homotopy theory and the study of function spaces.

label: Modes of Convergence
notes: Pointwise limits of continuous functions need not be continuous, but uniform limits always are. Uniform convergence on compact sets gives the local control that preserves continuity on locally compact domains. Distinguishing these modes clarifies when limits behave well.
